about: Block Square on a sale night: what stands where, who is there, what they say and what is called from the Block. Read by Tools/build_town_level.py (GUT_TOWN_LIST=Tools/town_block_square.json Tools/build_town_level.sh). Places are in the map's own metres (x east, y north), from for-review/design/map-of-ashmarket.md; 'yaw' and 'facing' are compass bearings (0 north, 90 east, 180 south, 270 west). STAGE 2: the Block's trailer, its lamps, the ramp, the tables, the scale, the rope, the Holding Yard's truck beds and the counting house are models made in Mixar for it (ArtSource/mixar/square_*), and its board, bills and marks are pictures made there.
name: Block Square
errand: The Block is selling. The way in is the gap in the rope.
To buy a fighter: Margin, at the table.
To borrow or pay: Mother Ledger.
Back to the Gut: north, up the lane.
Main Street: south, past the Warden.
The Velvet Tin: west, between the buses and the stack.
walk_about: The ground that can be walked on. Each patch runs on into whatever stands along its edge (a wall, a row of containers, a fence), and that is what stops whoever walks: the builder measures every model and refuses a place where a patch ends at nothing.
rows_about: Containers end to end, stacked. 'face' is the line their near sides stand on, 'side' the side of it they lie on, and they are spread between 'from' and 'to'. The blue one's awning is on its own left, so 'yaw' is chosen to turn it to the street.

bulbs_about: Candelas. The camera is set for the floodlit cage (see NightExposure in Tools/build_gut_content.py), so a bulb that is to light a wall three metres off wants some thousands.

lot_down_about: The way somebody the player has bought comes down to them: from the head of the deck along behind the numbers to the head of the other ramp, down it, and back out of the buyers to the strip the clerk's table stands in. From there they follow the player.
lot_way_about: The way the lots come up: from the head of the file they are kept in, in the Holding Yard, to the foot of the ramp, to the head of the deck. The file runs back east from its first place. 'lot_aisle' is how far behind its number a lot walks along the line of the others.

people.name: Margin
people.prompt: Talk to Margin, the Block's clerk

lines.words: Lot list is on the board, and the book is here. If you are buying, I write your name against theirs, and they sleep in your yard tonight. The Chainmen's fifth is in the price already. Are you buying?

answers.words: Show me who is for sale.
Where do they go when I have bought them?

lines.words: Eighteen litres, and six more for each thing they know how to do, before anybody bids. A fighter with a name costs what the Gut says they cost.

With you. They follow whoever holds their paper, as far as your yard beside the Gut. The yard gate is on Pool Street, past the fighters' door: the yard hand lets owners in. You train them there, and you send them down into the pool from there.
I lend twenty-five and I write thirty-five. I like to begin with the figures.
lines.note: Her page for you: {owed} L owed. You are holding {held} L.

answers.words: Take what I owe out of what I hold.

lines.words: Twenty-five litres, counted out. Thirty-five written down.
lines.note: Her page for you: {owed} L owed. You are holding {held} L.

lines.words: No. A hundred and five litres is as much as I let anybody owe me, and you know where debts are paid here.
lines.note: Her page for you: {owed} L owed. You are holding {held} L.

lines.words: Your page is clean. I take nothing I am not owed.
lines.note: Her page for you: {owed} L owed. You are holding {held} L.

lines.words: With what? You are holding nothing.
lines.note: Her page for you: {owed} L owed. You are holding {held} L.

lines.words: Struck off. I have written it down.
lines.note: {dealt} Her page for you: {owed} L owed. You are holding {held} L.

lines.words: I have no page for you. Put water on a fight at Chalk's window first, and then I will know your face.
People who signed. I have never collared anybody. People sign. I only remember it for them.

Main Street is open as far as the Gate Yard. The armorers and the gunsmith are down it, if you have business with either. Hands where the Chainmen can see them, or you lose one. I am not shitting you.

doors.prompt: West along Tin Lane, to the Velvet Tin

bidding_about: What Caller Strand says while a lot is bid for at the table, in the pieces it is recorded in: every figure a bid can come to (4 to 160), each buyer, each turn of phrase. A call has a figure in it, so none can be recorded whole: the game says the pieces end to end (ATownGameMode::SayAuction). Each is a recording bid_<name> beside his other calls. 25 November.

clips.who_opens: Who opens? Who starts me at
clips.no_bid: No bid. Back on the book.

calls_about: What Caller Strand calls from the Block, round and round. Nobody speaks it: there is no voice for it, so it is written up on the screen. 'stirs' is a lot knocked down, which gets something out of the crowd. Prices follow the numbers pass: 18 L and 6 L for each skill, before bidding. 'lot' is the lot a call is about, from its being put up to the clerk's writing it down: none of them is called once the player has bought that lot and led it away. 'sells' is the lot a call knocks down: it is walked off the Block, down the ramp, to the file kept in the Holding Yard. 'brings_up' walks every lot that is kept back up to its number.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Lot one. A man, twenty-six, sound in wind and limb. Digs, hauls, and has swung a club for money.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Thirty litres opens. Thirty. Who starts me?

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Thirty at the rope. Thirty-five, the Gut's man. Forty, at the back.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Forty-five? Forty-five, Mr Rask. Going at forty-five.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Sold. Forty-five litres, to Mr Rask of the Gut.

calls.speaker: Margin, at the table
calls.words: Lot one, forty-five litres, to H. Rask. Nine to the book.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Lot two. A woman, thirty-one. Reads, figures, and sews a straight seam. Three things on the card.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Thirty-six opens, and cheap at it. Thirty-six, the Tin. Forty.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Forty-four, the Pump office. Forty-eight, the Tin again. Any more?

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Sold. Forty-eight litres, to the Velvet Tin.

calls.speaker: Margin, at the table
calls.words: Lot two, forty-eight litres, to the Tin. Nine and a half to the book.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Lot three. A man, nineteen. Strong as he looks and knows nothing yet. Somebody will teach him.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Eighteen opens. Eighteen, the Scrappers. Twenty.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Twenty-two. Twenty-two once. Nobody? He eats less than a dog.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Sold. Twenty-two litres, to the Scrappers' guild.

calls.speaker: Margin, at the table
calls.words: Lot three, twenty-two litres, to the guild. Four and a half to the book.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Lot four. A woman, twenty-four. Cooks, and can strip a pump and put it back. Two on the card.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Thirty opens. Thirty, the Pump office. Thirty-four, at the rope.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Thirty-eight, the Pump. Forty-two. Forty-two, and the Pump shakes its head.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Sold. Forty-two litres, to the bidder at the rope.

calls.speaker: Margin, at the table
calls.words: Lot four, forty-two litres. Name, please. Eight and a half to the book.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Lot five. A man, thirty-five, heavy. Hauls for two and has stood in a ring and walked out of it.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Thirty opens. Thirty-five, Mr Rask. Forty, the Scrappers.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Forty-five, Mr Rask. Fifty. Fifty, Mr Rask, and that is the Gut's water talking.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Sold. Fifty litres, to Mr Rask of the Gut.

calls.speaker: Margin, at the table
calls.words: Lot five, fifty litres, to H. Rask. Ten to the book.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Lot six. A woman, twenty-eight. Reads, and keeps a count. Signed for her brother's water and here she stands.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Thirty opens. Thirty, the Tin. Thirty-four, the Pump office.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Thirty-eight? Thirty-eight, the Pump. Going at thirty-eight.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Sold. Thirty-eight litres, to the Pump office.

calls.speaker: Margin, at the table
calls.words: Lot six, thirty-eight litres, to the Pump. Seven and a half to the book.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: That is the six. Hold your water: the next six are at the wash, and they come up when they are clean.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Six more. Up the ramp and onto your numbers.

calls.speaker: Margin, at the table
calls.words: Second six. The book is open, and water is weighed before a hand is shaken.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Look them over while they walk. Backs, hands, teeth. Nothing past the rope.

calls.speaker: Caller Strand
calls.words: Settle. Settle. Eyes on the Block.

sky_about: Where the dome the night sky is painted in is centred, how big it is, and where its own ground lies. The cage's own dome ends at the square's south-west corner, and Main Street is beyond it.
finds_about: What lies about to be found and picked up (E, or X): a good by the name the town knows it by, where it lies on the map, and which way it is turned. Each is there once: picked up, it is in the bag and gone from the street for good.
